title: Verify Pyodide Blob conversion in the real browser before relying on Python mocks
applies_when: Python code running under Pyodide passes bytes, lists or option dictionaries into JavaScript Blob/XMLHttpRequest APIs. A native Python test can check call arguments but cannot establish the browser's proxy-conversion behavior.
lesson: Use a small real module-worker and loopback echo check before finalizing the fix. Pyodide can proxy Python bytes rather than turn them into a JavaScript byte buffer: a Blob built from an unconverted list containing bytes can send the Python repr, not the bytes. Explicitly convert Blob parts with pyodide.ffi.to_js and option dictionaries with dict_converter=Object.fromEntries; use a string 'type' key. Check received bytes and Content-Type, not merely Blob constructor arguments. Follow the actual upper caller too: fsspec HTTPFileSystem.put_file supplies a finite chunk iterator. Wrapping that iterator in [data] still sends its repr, even after direct bytes/JSON requests pass; consume its chunks as Blob parts before conversion, then check round-trip bytes, progress counters and caller-owned stream lifetime. This is buffering, not streaming. Keep JSON serialization separate from interop: serialize the JSON value itself and distinguish omitted None from supported falsy values such as {}, [], False, 0 and ''. Retain no-body and conflicting-input controls, verify the imported production source, then add focused native mocks for the conversion protocol. Real browser checks and mock-based regression checks answer different questions.
avoid_when: This is not guidance to add Pyodide to ordinary CPython requests, or to require a browser for every Python bug. A mocked to_js identity function does not qualify actual JavaScript conversion. The observed runtime is Pyodide314.0.7/CPython3.14.2; other versions, binary payload families, cloud endpoints, browser policies and response paths need applicable checks. Do not buffer unbounded iterators or infer large-upload memory safety from tiny payloads. Worker XHR results do not establish main-thread synchronous-XHR support. Nineteen loopback checks and a native test-file pass do not prove full CI, universal correctness, speedup or a prospective evidence-selector advantage. Do not overwrite a valid caller's explicitly selected content-type policy merely because this particular shim had no such policy.

evidence.note: Official documentation distinguishes implicit conversion from proxying and documents explicit conversion. In particular, Python bytes are proxied to preserve round-trip type identity; a constructor accepting an object is not proof that it received the intended byte buffer. The stable documentation version can change.
The to_js API supports explicit conversion and a dict_converter. Choose the conversion expected by the actual JavaScript API instead of assuming a Python mapping is a JavaScript options object.

Original browser observations: object JSON sent null, five falsy JSON values sent no body, and b'hello' sent its repr with no MIME type. The first repair passed nine direct-browser checks and 65 native tests but still corrupted all eight actual put_file round trips. The later submitted head passes 19 browser expectations, including eight POST/PUT x file/BytesIO x binary/empty round trips, and 67 native tests. The same new test file on the partial head has two failures and 65 passes. Native mocks check protocol only; acceptance/CI, large-file memory and performance are not claimed.

Pinned partial repair serializes supplied JSON and converts direct Blob parts/options. It still wraps the upper caller's generator as a single Blob part. Direct browser and native tests at that stage did not qualify actual chunked uploads; retain this negative state rather than treating the original nine passes as universal correctness.

The follow-up in the same PR consumes finite Iterator chunks as Blob parts before conversion. Actual loopback put_file/cat_file controls check non-UTF8 bytes, empty files, POST/PUT, filesystem/BytesIO sources, completed progress counts and retained caller stream ownership. The buffered strategy does not claim incremental streaming or bounded large-file memory.
